internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The verb-and-adjective cluster carries the image transparently. Bare I = erect standing/rising: "when they stood up (qāmū)" 18:14; "stand before God devoutly (qūmū)" 2:238; "arise and warn (qum)" 74:2; "the Day people stand before the Lord (yaqūmu)" 83:6; "the Day the Spirit and angels stand in rows" 78:38; and the striking antonym pairings that fix the sense as ERECT posture specifically — "standing (qiyāman) and sitting (quʿūdan) and on their sides" 3:191 & 4:103, "prostrate and standing (qiyāman)" 25:64, "then they are standing (qiyāmun), looking" 39:68. Form IV = cause-to-stand → erect/establish/maintain: literally "he set it (the leaning wall) upright (fa-aqāmahu)" 18:77; then metaphorically "keep up the prayer (aqīmū al-ṣalāt)" (dozens, e.g. 2:3, 2:43, 4:103), "maintain the limits of God (yuqīmā ḥudūd Allāh)" 2:229–230, "keep up the weighing with justice (aqīmū al-wazn)" 55:9, "uphold the Torah and Gospel (aqāmū)" 5:66/5:68, "establish the religion (aqīmū al-dīn)" 42:13, "set your face upright toward the religion (aqim wajhaka)" 10:105/30:30/30:43. Form X = keep straight/steadfast: "remain upright as commanded (fa-staqim)" 11:112, "kept straight on the path (istaqāmū)" 41:30/46:13/72:16, "as long as they stay true (istaqāmū) to you, stay true to them" 9:7. The straightness family is the same erect line abstracted: "straight path (ṣirāṭ mustaqīm)" (very frequent, e.g. 1:6, 6:153), "the straight balance (al-qisṭās al-mustaqīm)" 17:35/26:182, "the upright religion (al-dīn al-qayyim)" 12:40/30:30/9:36, "a straight religion (dīnan qiyaman)" 6:161, the Book "straight, without crookedness (qayyiman)" 18:2, "which is most upright (aqwam)" 17:9, "more upright in speech" 73:6, "best conformation (aḥsan taqwīm)" 95:4. The subsist/endure/uphold branch is internally bridged: God "the Self-Subsisting (al-Qayyūm)" 2:255/3:2/20:111; "standing over (qāʾiman ʿalā) every soul" 13:33; "upholding justice (qāʾiman bi-l-qisṭ)" 3:18; "maintainers over women (qawwāmūna)" 4:34; "steadfast upholders of justice (qawwāmīna bi-l-qisṭ)" 4:135/5:8; "lasting punishment (ʿadhāb muqīm)" 5:37/9:68/11:39/42:45; property "which God made a mainstay (qiyāman) for you" 4:5 and the Kaaba "a mainstay (qiyāman) for people" 5:97; heaven and earth "stand/subsist (taqūma) by His command" 30:25. The place/event branch: "the standing-place of Abraham (maqām Ibrāhīm)" 2:125/3:97, "a praiseworthy station (maqāman maḥmūdan)" 17:79, "who fears the standing before his Lord (maqāma rabbihi)" 55:46/79:40, "two others stand in their stead (maqāmahumā)" 5:107, and the eschatological nominalization "the Day of Standing/Resurrection (yawm al-qiyāmah)" (dozens). Finally qawm "people" (the great bulk of the N tokens, e.g. "the people of Noah" 71:1, "O my people (yā qawmi)" 11:50, "the wrongdoing people (al-qawm al-ẓālimīn)" 5:51) reads as a collective constituted to stand-together as one body — the group aspect of the same "standing/upholding" image that is explicitly attested in qiyāman 'mainstay', qawwāmūn 'upholders', al-Qayyūm and muqīm.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Subtracting FORM: I = enter/hold the erect state (qāma); IV = put-into-the-erect-state → erect/establish/keep-up (aqāma); X = hold-oneself-to-the-erect/straight line → be steadfast (istaqāma); intensives qawwām/al-Qayyūm = one who constantly stands/upholds; participles qāʾim/muqīm = the one standing/enduring; verbal nouns qiyām/maqām/muqām/iqāmah/qiyāmah = the act, place, or event of standing; adjectives qayyim/aqwam/mustaqīm/taqwīm = the quality of the held-upright/straight line. Subtracting CONSTRUCTION: aqāma + al-ṣalāt = 'keep up'; qāma + ilā = 'rise toward'; qāma/qāʾim + bi- (bi-l-qisṭ) = 'uphold/maintain'; qāʾim + ʿalā = 'stand over/oversee'; istaqāma + ʿalā/ilā/li- = 'keep straight on/toward/true to'; khāfa + maqām = 'fear the standing-before'. Subtracting PARTICIPANTS (who stands: prophet, believers, a people, the Hour, heaven and earth, palm trees on their roots 59:5, God) and CONTEXT (ritual: prayer; eschatology: al-qiyāmah, the witnesses standing 40:51, the reckoning standing 14:41; law: ḥudūd, testimony 65:2, weights/measures 55:9; narrative: prophets addressing their qawm). What survives every subtraction is: erect/upright standing, assumed and held.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: qawm "a people/folk" (the dominant nominal, e.g. 71:1:5:1 "qawmihi", 11:50:6:2 "yā qawmi", 5:51:21:2 "al-qawm al-ẓālimīn"). Here the erect-standing residue is NOT surface-recoverable in the individual token — "the people of Noah" does not read off "standing." It reconciles only through a derivational/etymological bridge: a qawm is a collective constituted to stand-together as one social body. Crucially, that bridge IS partly attested inside this very corpus, where the same root yields the abstract "standing/upholding/subsisting": qiyāman = a mainstay by which people stand (4:5, 5:97), qawwāmūn = upholders (4:34, 4:135, 5:8), al-Qayyūm = the self-standing sustainer of all (2:255), muqīm = the enduring/standing (5:37). Because qawm nonetheless requires this inferential step rather than surfacing the image directly, it is the single hardest case and the reason the unity is graded MODERATE rather than STRONG — but the residue is neither absent nor contradicted, so it is reconciled, not anomalous.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative core is generic "firmness / fixity / steadfast establishment" (a thbt-like 'be firmly set'), which would also cover establishing, subsisting, and staying-the-course, and would arguably smooth the qawm case ('a fixed/constituted entity'). Internal evidence arbitrates AGAINST it and in favor of the more specific "erect/upright standing": (1) the explicit antonym contrasts qiyāman vs quʿūdan 'sitting' (3:191, 4:103), sujjadan vs qiyāman 'prostrate vs standing' (25:64), and qiyāmun 'standing [after being felled]' (39:68) show the root denotes the ERECT posture as opposed to sitting/prostrating/lying — a distinction mere 'firmness' cannot carry; (2) the whole straightness sub-family (mustaqīm 'straight [path]', qayyim/aqwam 'upright, without crookedness', taqwīm 'well-proportioned form') is the geometric image of the erect/vertical line, not of fixity. Fixity is thus a downstream consequence (a thing that keeps standing endures), not the center.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest neighbors and how qwm is distinct: (a) q-ʿ-d 'sit' — the direct antonym, co-attested with qwm in 3:191 and 4:103; qwm = up/erect, qʿd = down/seated. (b) th-b-t 'be firm/fixed' — used for immobility (e.g. 'make our feet firm', thabbit aqdāmanā 3:147); qwm adds the rising-to and the vertical/erect and straight dimensions that thbt lacks. (c) n-ṣ-b 'set up/plant erect [an object]' — overlaps with aqāma but centers on fixing an external object, whereas qwm centers on the self-standing/subsisting and owns the straightness family. (d) q-s-ṭ / ʿ-d-l / s-w-y 'justice / balance / evenness' — border on mustaqīm/qayyim, but note qāʾiman bi-l-qisṭ 3:18 pairs the two roots: qwm supplies 'standing/upholding', qisṭ supplies 'the justice'; qwm's rightness is the erect-straight LINE, not equity or levelness. Falsifiability: the hypothesis fails if any occurrence uses a qwm-form for sitting/reclining, for downward/collapsing motion, or for a meaning incompatible with erect-standing/uprightness/establishment, or if qawm ever denoted a non-collective/inanimate mass that cannot be construed as a constituted standing body. No such occurrence appears across the 660; qawm always denotes a human collective, and every verbal/adjectival token is construable as erect-standing/uprightness/keeping-up.

internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty residue — rising into and holding an erect, upright standing — is recoverable across all 660 occurrences after subtracting form, construction, participants, and context. It is surface-transparent and determinate for the entire verbal/adjectival/eschatological system: bare I 'stand/rise', IV 'erect/establish/keep-up' (with the literal anchor fa-aqāmahu 'he set the wall upright' 18:77), X 'stay straight/steadfast', the straightness set (mustaqīm, qayyim, aqwam, taqwīm), the subsist/uphold set (al-Qayyūm, qāʾim ʿalā, qawwām, muqīm, qiyāman-mainstay), and the station/standing/Resurrection nominals (maqām, qiyām, al-qiyāmah). The direction is fixed (concrete erect-standing → its extensions), and the root is sharply bounded by internal evidence — the qiyām/quʿūd (standing/sitting) antonymy pins the sense to ERECT posture and separates it from mere firmness (thbt), while qāʾiman bi-l-qisṭ shows the root supplies 'standing/upholding' and not the co-occurring 'justice'. The unity is graded MODERATE rather than STRONG for one honest reason: the dominant nominal qawm 'people' does not surface the standing image in each token and joins the core only through a derivational bridge (a collective constituted to stand together) — a bridge that is itself partly attested within the corpus by qiyāman 'mainstay', qawwāmūn 'upholders', al-Qayyūm and muqīm. Because in qawm the residue is inferential (never contradicted, never absent in the sense of denoting something antithetical to standing), no occurrence is placed in inconsistent_refs, and the disposition is a genuine but metaphorically-extended unity: PREFERRED / MODERATE.

adversarial_verification.notes:
Read all 660 occurrences (lines 1-4011). The frozen image (erect upright standing + keeping-so) is genuinely LIVE and distinctive across the whole derivational apparatus: finite verbs I (qāmū 18:14, qūmū 2:238, qum 74:2, yaqūmu 83:6/78:38), forms IV (aqāma-hu 18:77 lit. 'set it upright'; aqīmū al-ṣalāt; yuqīmā ḥudūd 2:229) and X (fa-staqim 11:112, istaqāmū 41:30); the straightness family (mustaqīm, aqwam 17:9/2:282/73:6, qayyim 12:40/30:30/9:36, qiyaman 6:161, taqwīm 95:4); the subsistence family (al-Qayyūm 2:255, qāʾim 13:33, muqīm 'lasting punishment', qawwām 4:34/4:135, qiyām 'mainstay' 4:5/5:97); and the place/event family (maqām Ibrāhīm 2:125, maqāman maḥmūdan 17:79, maqāma rabbihi 55:46, al-Qiyāmah). For this ~163-token cluster I found NO genuine failure; here distinctiveness is fine (separates from wqf 'halt', qʿd/jls 'sit', thbt 'be fixed', ʿdl 'justice').

REFUTATION VECTOR = qawm 'people' (form N, ~497/660 = 75% of tokens). The discovery itself fixes the image as specifically VERTICAL/ERECT posture (via the standing-vs-sitting-vs-prostrate antonym pairings), yet qawm carries no such live image: 'قوم نوح', 'يا قوم', 'القوم الظالمين' are a plain ethnic/social collective, functionally identical to ʾummah/nās/qabīlah/ṭāʾifah/malaʾ. The rescue ('a collective constituted to stand-together / the group aspect of the standing-upholding image') is ad-hoc and circular: it silently swaps the frozen 'erect posture' image for an abstract 'upholding' node, then attaches it to any group — nothing in qawm's usage activates it, and it fails to discriminate qawm from its neighbor collective-nouns. In several places context actively contradicts 'standing': 69:7 (القوم فيها صرعى — the people FALLEN dead like hollow palm-trunks), 7:64 (قوماً عمين 'a blind people'), 23:106 and 6:77 (قوماً/القوم ضالّين 'a straying people' — juxtaposing qawm with the antonym of the root's OWN straightness pole, mustaqīm/aqwam).

HARDEST CASE + RESOLUTION: A defender invokes the classical etymology (qawm = 'those who rise/undertake affairs', with 49:11's qawm-vs-nisāʾ contrast and internal witnesses qiyām 'mainstay', qawwām 'upholder'). This is why the verdict is NOT REFUTED: qawm is etymologically inside qwm, so this is polysemy with a bleached branch, not homonymy — the candidate CAN bridge it. But the bridge is only a dead/etymological tie, not the LIVE, specific 'erect vertical standing' image the candidate claims for EVERY occurrence; the single frozen image is thus over-specified relative to qawm and non-discriminating there. That is precisely an over-breadth / underdetermined-core failure → PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED.
